findings.issue: Interface is missing 5 methods declared in query/fiado.sql: GetCustomerByUserIDAndID, ListPendingFiadoSalesByCustomer, SummarizePendingFiadoSalesByCustomer. Generated code fiado.sql.go does not exist. Either sqlc was not run or failed. Code references db.GetCustomerByUserIDAndIDParams, db.ListPendingFiadoSalesByCustomerParams, etc. which do not exist. This will fail to compile.

Subquery over payments table has no WHERE clause filtering by user_id. While technically safe due to outer join filtering, this violates defense-in-depth: aggregates all payments globally then filters. Should add user_id filter to subquery or use alternative join strategy.

Three separate DB calls (GetCustomerByUserIDAndID, SummarizePendingFiadoSalesByCustomer, ListPendingFiadoSalesByCustomer) without transaction. Concurrent modifications could cause snapshot inconsistency between calls—e.g., if a payment is made between summary and list calls, pagination totals may not match data. Should wrap in transaction or document isolation requirements.

GetCustomerByUserIDAndID returns ~10 columns (id, user_id, name, document, phone, email, address, active, created_at, updated_at) but only the error is checked; customer data is discarded with `_`. Inefficient and confusing. Should either use a smaller query (EXISTS or COUNT) or actually use the returned customer data.

Discards bool return value from timestamptzTime(row.SaleDate) with `_`. If saleDate is NULL in database, silently returns time.Time{} (zero value) without indication. Should either handle the bool or propagate the error to prevent silent data corruption.
Duplicated struct definition. Also defined in packages/api-go/internal/sync/types.go:169. Should extract to shared package or reuse sync.FailureResponse.

Error handling creates new apperror.New without wrapping the original strconv.Atoi error with %w. Per AGENTS.md rule 'Wrap inspectable errors with %w', should be `fmt.Errorf(...: %w, err)` to allow error inspection up the call stack.

Error handling creates new apperror.New without wrapping the original strconv.ParseInt error with %w. Per AGENTS.md rule 'Wrap inspectable errors with %w', should be `fmt.Errorf(...: %w, err)` to allow error inspection up the call stack.

Silent error handling: if n.Float64Value() returns error OR !f.Valid, returns 0 without indication. Calling code at line 57, 81, 82, 83 silently gets 0 for invalid amounts. Per AGENTS.md guidelines, errors should be propagated or logged; callers should know when data is invalid.
